turnaround_reason: Zoetis, the animal-health leader, de-rated ~51% from its 52-week high (to near the $71 low) after cutting 2026 guidance twice on softening U.S. companion-animal demand — fewer vet visits, price-sensitive pet owners, and rising competition. The debate is temporary demand air-pocket versus structural growth reset.
bullish_points: Best-in-class quality of the whole batch: 71.7% gross margin, 40.7% operating margin, 27.7% net margin — a genuine compounder now on sale
Category leader with a broad, durable franchise (Simparica, Librela, livestock) and pricing power over time
Librela trends stabilizing in the U.S. after a -22% quarter; management sees traction from fixes
Livestock/cattle demand strong (New World screwworm response) providing an offset to companion-animal softness
Trading near a 52-week low with a still-growing secular animal-health end market
bearish_points: Guidance cut is real: 2026 revenue lowered to $9.12-9.32B, organic revenue -3% to -1%, adjusted net income -9% to -5% — earnings are declining, not just decelerating
Core U.S. companion-animal revenue down 11%; if vet-visit weakness is structural (GLP-1-style behavior shifts, macro) the reset is deeper
Still not cheap on absolute multiples for a company guiding to declining EPS
Total debt $9.26B vs $1.68B cash; manageable for this cash flow but not trivial
Dossier technicals null — no confirmed base, could re-break lower on another guide-down
catalyst: Stabilization/reacceleration of U.S. companion-animal demand and Librela recovery, confirmed in the next 1-2 earnings prints; any guidance raise would re-rate a quality name off a trough multiple
suggested_trade: Starter spot position (small-to-medium) near the low; scale on a confirmed guidance stabilization
key_risk: A third consecutive guidance cut showing the U.S. companion-animal softness is structural rather than cyclical
would_skip_if: Next print cuts guidance again or U.S. companion-animal revenue declines accelerate
